answer: ﻿A reputation bond is a haven earned slowly: each peer-graded epoch adds a layer of verified work, and the stake cannot be borrowed or transferred. A gale of fresh aliases arrives at the wharf with nothing — no history, no weight, no path to full standing that skips the queue. A farm must grow every clone through the same serial accumulation; there is no pooling mechanism that lets one deep history lift the rest, so the cost per alias stays flat and the hundredth fake is as expensive as the first.
